mechanism_narrative: A further weekly decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals fewer commuting-linked stops and less incidental shopping, so RETAIL_REC will keep falling over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below the current four-week mean for at least three of those weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, people substitute home-based routines for discretionary trips, depressing retail visits within one week and keeping RETAIL_REC lower on average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -40 for a weekly mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above +10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week after TRANSIT is below -40 and RESIDENTIAL is above +10, or it rebounds above the last four-week average within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained worsening in GROCERY_PHARM alongside lower RETAIL_REC indicates households are consolidating outings into essential trips, which reduces discretionary retail frequency and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM drops by at least 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: After two consecutive weekly drops in GROCERY_PHARM, RETAIL_REC does not stay below its current four-week mean over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and TRANSIT are both weak at the same time, public movement is broadly compressed rather than shifted outdoors, so retail mobility will continue to deteriorate across the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days while both PARKS and TRANSIT stay below their current weekly levels for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week stabilization in TRANSIT after a prior sharp drop can precede a modest rebound in retail trips as essential commuting resumes, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stops falling and posts a weekly increase after being below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to fall for the next week after TRANSIT turns upward from below -40, or no rebound appears within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES recover while RESIDENTIAL softens, daytime exposure rises and people add discretionary stops before or after work, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above its prior two-week average while RESIDENTIAL falls below its prior two-week average
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last four-week average over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent winter mobility slump in PARKS and TRANSIT signals broad caution and fewer out-of-home trips, which suppresses discretionary retail visits for the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its current four-week mean within two weeks despite PARKS and TRANSIT remaining depressed.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both cross into a stronger recovery band together, the combined reopening effect will first raise footfall near stations and offices, then lift retail mobility over the following month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 10 points and WORKPLACES improves by at least 8 points within one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below the last four-week mean for the full 28 days after simultaneous improvements in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.
